smells.finding: No added function exceeds ~25 statements. The largest bodies are _unbound_refusal (17) and _log (16); main() grew by 10 lines inside its existing dispatch chain. Docstrings are long, but docstring length is not method length -- that is the comments-as-deodorant entry below.
The server module declares no classes. The two added test classes are 3 and 5 methods.
_calllog / _start_marker / _rejectionlog are three one-line wrappers over _telemetry_path, and _HOW_TO_BIND / _HOW_TO_REBIND differ by one word.

override.repo_standard: global-everyone.md, Universal posture: 'One canonical path; no speculative abstraction' and 'one name for one thing (docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md)'
override.reason: The shared logic IS extracted -- _telemetry_path is the single predicate, and each wrapper is a one-line named binding whose only content is its env var, its filename and the documentation the deleted module constant used to carry. Collapsing the three into one call site would delete three names the rest of the repo refers to by name, which is the opposite of one-name-for-one-thing. The two message constants are deliberately distinct because the review handoff makes the wording split load-bearing: an unbound door must name no path, a named-but-unusable one must name it.

smells.finding: _rebind_refusal reaches into checklist_engine._active_lease -- a PRIVATE function of another module -- to decide whether this door holds a live lease. That is inappropriate intimacy across a module boundary: the door now depends on an engine internal with no published contract, so an engine-side rename breaks the door silently rather than at a declared seam. The implementer's justification is sound (re-deriving 'is this lease live' would drift from the engine's own reading) and I agree the trade is right today, so this is an observation, not a blocker -- it wants promoting to a public engine accessor if a third caller appears. The implementer already recorded it as their own triage candidate 3.

SPINE_FILE and SPINE_SESSION travel together into _bind_process_to and back out of open_work, but a pair is below the clump threshold and they are already named as one thing ('both identity roots') in the docstring and the pin.
_bind_process_to(spine_file: str, session: str) takes two bare strings where a Binding value object would be more typed.

override.repo_standard: global-crew.md, Implementation discipline: 'Make the minimal change that satisfies the handoff; no speculative abstraction.'
override.reason: There is exactly one caller and exactly one producer of these two values (open_work's return dict). A Binding type would be a one-use abstraction, and the module-wide AST pin already gives the property a type would have been introduced to protect -- that these two names are assigned in exactly two places.

smells.finding: Widest added signature is three parameters (_report_dropped_telemetry(target, exc, lost)). _resolve_confined kept its two keyword-only parameters; the change altered a default, not the arity.

The opposite is true here by design: the fail-closed decision is ONE predicate (_unbound_refusal) asked at two call sites -- main()'s tools/call dispatch for the whole surface, and run_engine as defence in depth. Adding a twelfth tool requires no new refusal code.

The module changes for telemetry placement, engine resolution, identity binding and dispatch in one commit, which looks divergent, but all four follow from a single reason: the door's identity became movable, so everything derived from it had to stop being derived once at import.
The longest chains are Path(__file__).resolve().parent and SPINE.parent -- navigation on a value type, not a train of collaborator lookups.
BINDS_WITHOUT_A_BOUND_SPINE is a set with exactly one member, where `nm != 'spine_open'` would do, and it is a hand-maintained list of exempt tool names.

override.repo_standard: CREW_CONTEXT.md, Verification Discipline: 'Define a guard by its consumer's behaviour, not by a hand-maintained list ... a list drifts from the predicate the code actually applies, AND THE GAP IS SILENT.'
override.reason: The standard's own stated rationale is the silence of the gap, and here the gap is not silent: a future binding tool omitted from the set is visibly REFUSED, never silently exempted -- the failure lands closed, which is this gate's whole thesis. Weighed against that, the set buys what the comparison cannot: the exemption is a listed fact a reader finds at the top of the dispatch rather than a `!=` buried inside it. I record the tension rather than dismissing it.

smells.finding: The house style here is heavy explanatory docstrings (the pre-existing _identity_violation is the same), and matching it is what CREW_CONTEXT.md asks for -- so volume alone is not the finding. The finding is that three of these docstrings have now DRIFTED from the code they explain, which is the failure mode this smell actually names, in a repo whose own standard says 'docstrings are hand-authored and none is checked against what runs': (1) _log_rejection:685 still says it appends to REJECTIONLOG, an identifier this same commit deleted; (2) _spine_open:962-963 still says the root comes from 'ambient SPINE_FILE, re-read fresh', which is precisely the os.environ read this commit removed; (3) examples/mcp-interactive-demo/README.md:69 still cites test_mcp_json_referenced_spine_file_exists_and_loads, renamed by this same commit. Where prose carries this much of the design, drifting prose is a defect in the design record, not a cosmetic issue. Reported in full under r4-quality.
